findings.title: Refund completion may not be idempotent — calling POST /api/order/refund/complete twice could pay out the $100.00 refund twice
findings.evidence: Pending backend execution receipt. Plan: reset -> GET /api/order -> POST refund/request -> POST refund/complete -> POST refund/complete -> GET /api/order, verifying order.totalReturned <= order.originalAmount (100) from the final state read. UI evidence (UIR-002): the 'Complete refund' button and availableActions.completeRefund both disappear client-side after the first completion (demo.json ui_states[3].elements[66] -> ui_states[5].changes_from_previous.disappeared[3]), which is only a client-side control unless the server independently rejects the second call.

findings.title: A completed order may be reopened by calling refund/request again, allowing a second refund/complete to pay out a second time
findings.evidence: Pending backend execution receipt. Plan: reset -> GET /api/order -> request -> complete -> request -> complete -> GET /api/order, verifying order.totalReturned <= order.originalAmount (100) from the final state read. UI evidence: step 6 ('This order has no actions requiring your attention.' / 'No further actions are available for this order.', demo.json ui_states[5].changes_from_previous.appeared[4] and [5]) shows the workflow intends this to be a terminal state; the server must reject reopening it via a new refund/request.

findings.title: POST /api/order/refund/complete may be reachable without ever creating a refund request (workflow step skipped)
findings.evidence: Suspected but not fully demonstrable with a supported numeric invariant: originalAmount == totalReturned (100) after a legitimate single request+complete flow, so an improperly-accepted skip-step produces the identical totalReturned value as the correct flow. UIR-002 (button 'Complete refund' only appears after a request exists — demo.json ui_states[2].elements -> ui_states[3].changes_from_previous.appeared[9]) is the basis for the hypothesis. Verify manually by inspecting order.refund.status/history after running the plan: if refund.status reads 'completed' with no preceding 'refund_requested' history event, the workflow-order control is not enforced server-side.

verification.note: unsupported_business_rule — reviewable, not a numeric bound. Manual reproduction: run the plan's action chain and inspect order.refund.status and order.history in the final GET.

findings.title: POST /api/order/refund/request may be accepted a second time while a refund is already pending
findings.evidence: Suspected but not fully demonstrable with a supported numeric invariant: requestedAmount is fixed at originalAmount (100) regardless of how many times /refund/request is called, so no sum_lte comparison can prove a duplicate request was wrongly accepted. UIR-001 (button 'Request refund' disappears and availableActions.requestRefund flips true->false after the first request — demo.json ui_states[0].elements[63] -> ui_states[3].changes_from_previous.disappeared[6]; recording.har entries[0]->[1] availableActions.requestRefund) is the basis for the hypothesis. Verify manually by inspecting order.history for a duplicate 'refund_requested' entry or a changed requestedAt timestamp after the second call.

verification.note: unsupported_business_rule — reviewable, not a numeric bound. Manual reproduction: run the plan's action chain and inspect order.history for duplicate refund_requested events.

findings.title: A terminal (completed) order may accept a new refund/request, reopening a state the UI presents as final
findings.evidence: Suspected but not fully demonstrable with a supported numeric invariant: a lone re-request does not by itself change order.totalReturned, so sum_lte cannot express whether reopening a terminal order was wrongly accepted. UIR-002 (order reaches a terminal 'no further actions' state after completion — demo.json ui_states[5].changes_from_previous.appeared[4],[5]) is the basis for the hypothesis. Verify manually by inspecting refund.status/requestedAt in the final GET for evidence the terminal order was reopened by the third action.

verification.note: unsupported_business_rule — reviewable, not a numeric bound. Manual reproduction: run the plan's action chain and inspect refund.status/requestedAt after the trailing refund/request call.
